title: CTS Denominations and the Gospel — Unit 9

blocks.en: 📖 Systematic Theology — Unit 9: Denominations, Authority, and the Gospel
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Teología Sistemática — Unidad 9: Denominaciones, Autoridad y el Evangelio

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace." — Ephesians 4:3 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Solícitos en guardar la unidad del Espíritu en el vínculo de la paz." — Efesios 4:3 (RVG)

blocks.en: Text: Ephesians 4:1-6 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Texto: Efesios 4:1-6

blocks.en: "I, therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you to walk worthy of the calling with which you were called, with all lowliness and gentleness, with longsuffering, bearing with one another in love, endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism; one God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all." — Ephesians 4:1-6
blocks.es_reference: "Yo pues, preso en el Señor, os ruego que andéis como es digno de la vocación con que fuisteis llamados, con toda humildad y mansedumbre, soportándoos con paciencia los unos a los otros en amor, solícitos en guardar la unidad del Espíritu en el vínculo de la paz. Un cuerpo, y un Espíritu, como fuisteis también llamados en una misma esperanza de vuestra vocación; un Señor, una fe, un bautismo, un Dios y Padre de todos, el cual es sobre todos, y por todos, y en todos." — Efesios 4:1-6

blocks.en: Day 1 — Unity, Not Uniformity
blocks.es_reference: Día 1 — Unidad, No Uniformidad

blocks.en: Our text calls for unity, but we must be careful not to mistake unity for uniformity. Uniformity is an external sameness where everyone looks, speaks, and acts in identical fashion. Unity, however, is a spiritual reality — a "bond of peace" that exists in the heart despite outward differences.
blocks.es_reference: Nuestro texto llama a la unidad, pero debemos tener cuidado de no confundir la unidad con la uniformidad. La uniformidad es una semejanza externa donde todos se ven, hablan y actúan de manera idéntica. La unidad, sin embargo, es una realidad espiritual — un "vínculo de paz" que existe en el corazón a pesar de las diferencias externas.

blocks.en: Today, we look at a landscape filled with thousands of denominations. It is estimated that there are as many as 500 different Baptist denominations alone. We in this church are non-denominational, but that does not mean we are "belief-less." We have deep, grounded convictions. We recognize that while we may sit on different branches, we are still part of the same massive family tree, with many brothers and sisters in Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Hoy, miramos un paisaje lleno de miles de denominaciones. Se estima que hay hasta 500 denominaciones Bautistas diferentes solamente. Nosotros en esta iglesia somos no denominacionales, pero eso no significa que estemos "sin creencias". Tenemos convicciones profundas y fundamentadas. Reconocemos que aunque podemos estar sentados en ramas diferentes, todavía somos parte del mismo gran árbol familiar, con muchos hermanos y hermanas en Cristo.

blocks.en: The Jerusalem Genesis: To understand the current state of the church, we must return to its birth. The first church in the New Testament was not found in Rome, Constantinople, Geneva, Wittenberg, or anywhere else we might name today. It was born in Jerusalem.
blocks.es_reference: El Origen en Jerusalén: Para entender el estado actual de la iglesia, debemos volver a su nacimiento. La primera iglesia en el Nuevo Testamento no se encontraba en Roma, Constantinopla, Ginebra, Wittenberg, ni en ningún otro lugar que podamos nombrar hoy. Nació en Jerusalén.

blocks.en: In that first assembly, there were no buildings. There were no denominations. There were no signs out front telling you what kind of church it was. There were no systems, no seminaries, and no centuries of developed, formalized theology. There were simply people — people who had seen the risen Christ, people who had been filled with the Holy Spirit, and people who were devoted to the apostles' teaching, to fellowship, to the breaking of bread, and to prayer. It was simple. It was powerful. It was alive.
blocks.es_reference: En esa primera asamblea, no había edificios. No había denominaciones. No había letreros afuera diciéndote qué tipo de iglesia era. No había sistemas, ni seminarios, ni siglos de teología desarrollada y formalizada. Había simplemente personas — personas que habían visto a Cristo resucitado, personas que habían sido llenas del Espíritu Santo, y personas que estaban dedicadas a la enseñanza de los apóstoles, a la comunión, al partimiento del pan y a la oración. Era simple. Era poderoso. Estaba vivo.

blocks.en: And yet — even there — there were differences. We sometimes imagine the early church as if everything was perfectly unified in every detail, but that is not what the New Testament shows us. Very early, questions began to arise: What do we do with Gentiles? Do they have to follow the law of Moses? What is essential, and what is not?
blocks.es_reference: Y sin embargo — incluso allí — había diferencias. A veces imaginamos la iglesia primitiva como si todo estuviera perfectamente unificado en cada detalle, pero eso no es lo que el Nuevo Testamento nos muestra. Muy temprano, comenzaron a surgir preguntas: ¿Qué hacemos con los gentiles? ¿Tienen que seguir la ley de Moisés? ¿Qué es esencial y qué no lo es?

blocks.en: These were not small questions. In Acts 15, the leaders of the church gathered together for a council. They came together not to dominate one another, but to discern truth. They listened. They reasoned. They testified of what God had done. And they came to a conclusion grounded in the Gospel. From the very beginning, the church was unified in Christ — but it was never without tension.
blocks.es_reference: Estas no eran preguntas pequeñas. En Hechos 15, los líderes de la iglesia se reunieron en un concilio. Se juntaron no para dominarse unos a otros, sino para discernir la verdad. Escucharon. Razonaron. Testificaron de lo que Dios había hecho. Y llegaron a una conclusión fundamentada en el Evangelio. Desde el principio, la iglesia estaba unificada en Cristo — pero nunca estuvo sin tensión.

blocks.en: Day 2 — The Great Divergence: Structure and Schism
blocks.es_reference: Día 2 — La Gran Divergencia: Estructura y Cisma

blocks.en: As history moved forward, what began as a Spirit-filled movement slowly developed into a formal structure. Leadership became more defined, authority became more centralized, and doctrine became more formalized. For many centuries, the dominant expression of Christianity became what we now call the Roman Catholic Church.
blocks.es_reference: A medida que la historia avanzaba, lo que comenzó como un movimiento lleno del Espíritu se desarrolló lentamente en una estructura formal. El liderazgo se hizo más definido, la autoridad se centralizó más, y la doctrina se formalizó más. Durante muchos siglos, la expresión dominante del cristianismo se convirtió en lo que ahora llamamos la Iglesia Católica Romana.

blocks.en: But even that unity did not last. Differences grew in language, culture, theology, and authority. Eventually, in 1054, a "Great Schism" took place between the church in Rome (the West) and the church in Constantinople (the East). The Western church continued as the Roman Catholic Church, while the Eastern church became the Eastern Orthodox Church — still present today in Greece, Russia, and throughout Eastern Europe.
blocks.es_reference: Pero incluso esa unidad no duró. Las diferencias crecieron en lenguaje, cultura, teología y autoridad. Eventualmente, en 1054, tuvo lugar un "Gran Cisma" entre la iglesia en Roma (el Occidente) y la iglesia en Constantinopla (el Oriente). La iglesia occidental continuó como la Iglesia Católica Romana, mientras que la iglesia oriental se convirtió en la Iglesia Ortodoxa Oriental — todavía presente hoy en Grecia, Rusia y por toda Europa Oriental.

blocks.en: Then came the great turning points of history: the printing press, the Renaissance, and the recovery of the Greek New Testament. Suddenly, people began to read the Bible for themselves. Before this, the Bible was often chained to the pulpit to keep ordinary people from reading and potentially misinterpreting it. But when the chains were broken, there was a spiritual explosion. Movements of reform rose across Europe. Men began to challenge traditions — not because they wanted something new, but because they wanted to return to something original. They wanted to come back to Scripture.
blocks.es_reference: Luego vinieron los grandes puntos de inflexión de la historia: la imprenta, el Renacimiento y la recuperación del Nuevo Testamento griego. De repente, las personas comenzaron a leer la Biblia por sí mismas. Antes de esto, la Biblia a menudo estaba encadenada al púlpito para evitar que la gente común la leyera y la malinterpretara potencialmente. Pero cuando las cadenas se rompieron, hubo una explosión espiritual. Movimientos de reforma se levantaron por toda Europa. Los hombres comenzaron a desafiar las tradiciones — no porque quisieran algo nuevo, sino porque querían volver a algo original. Querían regresar a las Escrituras.

blocks.en: From that came Protestantism, and from Protestantism came denominations. And that process has never stopped. Now, listen carefully: Not all differences are dangerous. Not all denominations are wrong. But not all teachings are harmless. Alongside legitimate expressions of Christianity, there have been movements that have gone so far that they have distorted the Gospel itself.
blocks.es_reference: De eso vino el Protestantismo, y del Protestantismo vinieron las denominaciones. Y ese proceso nunca se ha detenido. Ahora, escuchen con atención: No todas las diferencias son peligrosas. No todas las denominaciones están equivocadas. Pero no todas las enseñanzas son inofensivas. Junto con expresiones legítimas del cristianismo, ha habido movimientos que han ido tan lejos que han distorsionado el Evangelio mismo.

blocks.en: Groups like the Mormons and Jehovah's Witnesses do not simply differ — they redefine. They redefine Christ. They redefine salvation. They redefine the nature of God. And when the Gospel is changed, it is no longer the Gospel. The apostle Paul did not treat this lightly. He said in Galatians 1:9: "If anyone preaches any other gospel to you than what you have received, let him be accursed." The Gospel is not ours to improve or reshape.
blocks.es_reference: Grupos como los Mormones y los Testigos de Jehová no simplemente difieren — redefinen. Redefinen a Cristo. Redefinen la salvación. Redefinen la naturaleza de Dios. Y cuando el Evangelio es cambiado, ya no es el Evangelio. El apóstol Pablo no tomó esto a la ligera. Dijo en Gálatas 1:9: "Si alguno os predica diferente evangelio del que habéis recibido, sea anatema". El Evangelio no es nuestro para mejorarlo o remodelarlo.

blocks.en: Day 3 — The Catholic Church: Authority and the Foundation
blocks.es_reference: Día 3 — La Iglesia Católica: Autoridad y Fundamento

blocks.en: We begin with the Catholic Church — the largest and most historically influential branch of Christianity.
blocks.es_reference: Comenzamos con la Iglesia Católica — la rama más grande e históricamente influyente del cristianismo.

blocks.en: The Pope and the Rock: At the center of Catholic teaching is a claim built upon the words of Jesus at Caesarea Philippi in Matthew 16:13-18. Jesus asks His disciples, "Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?" They give various answers. Then He asks, "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answers: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." Jesus responds: "And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church..."
blocks.es_reference: El Papa y la Roca: En el centro de la enseñanza católica hay una afirmación construida sobre las palabras de Jesús en Cesarea de Filipo en Mateo 16:13-18. Jesús pregunta a Sus discípulos: "¿Quién dicen los hombres que es el Hijo del Hombre?" Dan varias respuestas. Entonces les pregunta: "¿Y vosotros quién decís que soy yo?" Pedro responde: "Tú eres el Cristo, el Hijo del Dios viviente". Jesús responde: "Y yo también te digo, que tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta roca edificaré mi iglesia..."

blocks.en: Catholic theology says: Peter is the rock. Peter is the first pope. And authority flows from him. But look again at the central issue in the passage: "Who do you say that I am?" Peter's answer — the truth of who Jesus is — is the "Rock." That revelation is the foundation of the church. Jesus is not building His church on a man; He is building His church on the truth of His own deity. Scripture confirms this: "For no other foundation can anyone lay than that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ" (1 Corinthians 3:11). The church is not anchored in Peter; it is anchored in Christ, the chief cornerstone (Ephesians 2:20).
blocks.es_reference: La teología católica dice: Pedro es la roca. Pedro es el primer papa. Y la autoridad fluye de él. Pero mire nuevamente la pregunta central del pasaje: "¿Y vosotros quién decís que soy yo?" La respuesta de Pedro — la verdad de quién es Jesús — es la "Roca". Esa revelación es el fundamento de la iglesia. Jesús no está edificando Su iglesia sobre un hombre; está edificando Su iglesia sobre la verdad de Su propia deidad. La Escritura confirma esto: "Porque nadie puede poner otro fundamento que el que está puesto, el cual es Jesucristo" (1 Corintios 3:11). La iglesia no está anclada en Pedro; está anclada en Cristo, la principal piedra del ángulo (Efesios 2:20).

blocks.en: The Priesthood and Mediation: Catholicism establishes a priesthood — a system where grace is mediated through an ordained class. While there were priests in the Old Testament, the New Testament says something radically different: "You... are a holy priesthood" (1 Peter 2:5). Every believer has direct access to God. Furthermore, 1 Timothy 2:5 says: "There is one God and one Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus." There are not many mediators; there is one. This means you can take your prayers and confessions directly to the throne of grace. You don't need a priest because you are a priest.
blocks.es_reference: El Sacerdocio y la Mediación: El catolicismo establece un sacerdocio — un sistema donde la gracia es mediada a través de una clase ordenada. Si bien había sacerdotes en el Antiguo Testamento, el Nuevo Testamento dice algo radicalmente diferente: "Vosotros... sois un sacerdocio santo" (1 Pedro 2:5). Cada creyente tiene acceso directo a Dios. Además, 1 Timoteo 2:5 dice: "Porque hay un solo Dios, y un solo mediador entre Dios y los hombres, Jesucristo hombre". No hay muchos mediadores; hay uno. Esto significa que puede llevar sus oraciones y confesiones directamente al trono de gracia. No necesita un sacerdote porque usted es un sacerdote.

blocks.en: The Treasury of Merit: There is the Catholic idea of "accumulated merit" from Jesus, Mary, and the saints. However, in the New Testament, every Christian was called a "saint." We are saints not because we are good, but because Jesus was good for us. Second, only Jesus was perfect. Everyone else, including Mary, was a sinner: "For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23). There is none that is righteous, no not one.
blocks.es_reference: El Tesoro de Méritos: Está la idea católica de "méritos acumulados" de Jesús, María y los santos. Sin embargo, en el Nuevo Testamento, cada cristiano era llamado un "santo". Somos santos no porque seamos buenos, sino porque Jesús fue bueno por nosotros. En segundo lugar, solo Jesús fue perfecto. Todos los demás, incluida María, fueron pecadores: "Por cuanto todos pecaron, y están destituidos de la gloria de Dios" (Romanos 3:23). No hay justo, ni aun uno.

blocks.en: The Sacraments and Tradition: The Catholic Church teaches that grace flows through the sacraments. But Scripture teaches: "For by grace you have been saved through faith... not of works" (Ephesians 2:8-9). Grace is not administered through ritual; it is received through faith. Finally, Catholic teaching places tradition alongside Scripture. But the Bible says it is sufficient on its own: "All Scripture is given by inspiration of God... that the man of God may be complete" (2 Timothy 3:16-17).
blocks.es_reference: Los Sacramentos y la Tradición: La Iglesia Católica enseña que la gracia fluye a través de los sacramentos. Pero la Escritura enseña: "Porque por gracia sois salvos por medio de la fe... no por obras" (Efesios 2:8-9). La gracia no se administra a través del ritual; se recibe a través de la fe. Finalmente, la enseñanza católica coloca la tradición junto con la Escritura. Pero la Biblia dice que es suficiente por sí sola: "Toda la Escritura es inspirada por Dios... a fin de que el hombre de Dios sea perfecto" (2 Timoteo 3:16-17).

blocks.en: Day 4 — Protestantism: Calvinism and the Reformed Tradition
blocks.es_reference: Día 4 — Protestantismo: Calvinismo y la Tradición Reformada

blocks.en: Now we come to John Calvin and the Reformed tradition. He was a brilliant mind and a systematic thinker. He had points and sub-points and sub-sub-points. He wrote the Institutes of the Christian Religion, shaping theology for generations. His teaching is summarized in the acronym TULIP:
blocks.es_reference: Ahora venimos a Juan Calvino y la tradición Reformada. Era una mente brillante y un pensador sistemático. Tenía puntos y subpuntos y sub-subpuntos. Escribió la Institución de la Religión Cristiana, dando forma a la teología por generaciones. Su enseñanza se resume en el acrónimo TULIP:

blocks.en: Total Depravity: Man is so affected by sin he cannot choose God on his own.
blocks.es_reference: Depravación Total: El hombre está tan afectado por el pecado que no puede elegir a Dios por sí mismo.

blocks.en: Unconditional Election: God chooses whom He will save based on His mercy.
blocks.es_reference: Elección Incondicional: Dios elige a quién salvará basado en Su misericordia.

blocks.en: Limited Atonement: Christ died specifically for the elect.
blocks.es_reference: Expiación Limitada: Cristo murió específicamente por los elegidos.

blocks.en: Irresistible Grace: When God calls, the soul will eventually respond.
blocks.es_reference: Gracia Irresistible: Cuando Dios llama, el alma eventualmente responderá.

blocks.en: Perseverance of the Saints: True believers will never fall away.
blocks.es_reference: Perseverancia de los Santos: Los verdaderos creyentes nunca caerán.

blocks.en: Reformed Balance and the Wider Protestant Family
blocks.es_reference: El Equilibrio Reformado y la Familia Protestante

blocks.en: The Danger of Balance and Predestination: There is truth here, but the danger is in what is emphasized beyond balance. Romans 8:29-30 and Ephesians 1:4-5 speak clearly of predestination. But some take this further and say God has predetermined some to heaven and some to hell. Scripture never says God is willing for people to perish; in fact, 2 Peter 3:9 says: "The Lord is not willing that any should perish..." God's sovereignty and God's heart are not in conflict.
blocks.es_reference: El Peligro del Equilibrio y la Predestinación: Hay verdad aquí, pero el peligro está en lo que se enfatiza más allá del equilibrio. Romanos 8:29-30 y Efesios 1:4-5 hablan claramente de la predestinación. Pero algunos llevan esto más lejos y dicen que Dios ha predeterminado a algunos para el cielo y a algunos para el infierno. La Escritura nunca dice que Dios está dispuesto a que las personas perezcan; de hecho, 2 Pedro 3:9 dice: "El Señor... no quiere que ninguno perezca...". La soberanía de Dios y el corazón de Dios no están en conflicto.

blocks.en: The Preservation of Urgency: There is a story of a Presbyterian who fell down the stairs. Bruised but alive, he picked himself up, dusted off his clothes, and said: "Well... thank God that's over with." It's a funny story, but it reveals a deeper issue. When everything is viewed as strictly predetermined, the sense of urgency often fades. This was seen in the history of missions. William Carey, a Baptist who is considered the father of modern missions, wanted to go to Asia. An older pastor stood up and said, "Sit down, young man; if God wants to save the heathen, he can do so without your help or mine." Carey refused that idea. Because he refused it, modern missions was born.
blocks.es_reference: La Preservación de la Urgencia: Hay una historia de un presbiteriano que se cayó por las escaleras. Magullado pero vivo, se levantó, se sacudió la ropa y dijo: "Bueno... gracias a Dios que eso terminó". Es una historia graciosa, pero revela un problema más profundo. Cuando todo se ve como estrictamente predeterminado, el sentido de urgencia a menudo se desvanece. Esto se vio en la historia de las misiones. William Carey, un Bautista considerado el padre de las misiones modernas, quería ir a Asia. Un pastor mayor se levantó y dijo: "Siéntate, joven; si Dios quiere salvar a los paganos, puede hacerlo sin tu ayuda o la mía". Carey rechazó esa idea. Debido a que la rechazó, nacieron las misiones modernas.

blocks.en: The Paradox of Growth: Nearly every modern spiritual awakening began with the Presbyterians. It was as if the Holy Spirit chose the most "closed" and restrictive group to move with His power. Hundreds of thousands were converted in these Awakenings. But interestingly, the Presbyterians did not experience the greatest growth. Growth exploded among Methodists and Baptists. The Methodists believed in our free will to accept God's offer of salvation. The Baptists, while often Calvinistic, were very practical (after all, these were new warm bodies for the pews and potential tithers). They didn't let a little theology get in the way of evangelism, eventually leading Baptists to become a "hybrid" of Calvinist and Arminian views.
blocks.es_reference: La Paradoja del Crecimiento: Casi cada despertar espiritual moderno comenzó con los Presbiterianos. Era como si el Espíritu Santo eligiera al grupo más "cerrado" y restrictivo para moverse con Su poder. Cientos de miles fueron convertidos en estos Despertares. Pero interesantemente, los Presbiterianos no experimentaron el mayor crecimiento. El crecimiento explotó entre los Metodistas y los Bautistas. Los Metodistas creían en nuestro libre albedrío para aceptar la oferta de salvación de Dios. Los Bautistas, aunque a menudo calvinistas, eran muy prácticos (después de todo, estos eran cuerpos cálidos nuevos para las bancas y diezmadores potenciales). No dejaron que un poco de teología se interpusiera en el camino del evangelismo, llevando eventualmente a los Bautistas a convertirse en un "híbrido" de las visiones calvinista y arminiana.

blocks.en: 💡 The Presbyterian on the Stairs: A Presbyterian fell down the stairs. Bruised but alive, he picked himself up, dusted off his clothes, and said: "Well... thank God that's over with." The story reveals that when everything is viewed as strictly predetermined, the sense of urgency often fades.
blocks.es_reference: 💡 El Presbiteriano en las Escaleras: Un presbiteriano se cayó por las escaleras. Magullado pero vivo, se levantó, se sacudió la ropa y dijo: "Bueno... gracias a Dios que eso terminó." La historia revela que cuando todo se ve como estrictamente predeterminado, el sentido de urgencia a menudo se desvanece.

blocks.en: Day 5 — The Arminian Pillar: Grace, Human Response, and Continuing Faith
blocks.es_reference: Día 5 — El Pilar Arminiano: Gracia, Respuesta Humana y Fe Continua

blocks.en: Alongside the Reformed tradition stands Arminianism, associated historically with Jacob Arminius and later strongly represented by John Wesley and the Methodist movement. It emphasizes both the necessity of divine grace and the genuine responsibility of the individual to respond to God in faith.
blocks.es_reference: Junto a la tradición Reformada está el Arminianismo, asociado históricamente con Jacobo Arminio y más tarde representado fuertemente por Juan Wesley y el movimiento metodista. Enfatiza tanto la necesidad de la gracia divina como la responsabilidad genuina del individuo de responder a Dios con fe.

blocks.en: Grace and Human Response: Classical Arminians agree that fallen humanity cannot save itself. They commonly speak of God’s prevenient grace as grace that enables a real response to the Gospel. The offer of salvation may therefore be accepted or resisted; faith is not produced by an irresistible decree. Calvinists answer that saving grace effectively brings the elect to faith. Both traditions intend to take seriously biblical teaching about grace, faith, human inability, and God’s sovereignty, but they arrange those truths differently.
blocks.es_reference: Gracia y Respuesta Humana: Los arminianos clásicos están de acuerdo en que la humanidad caída no puede salvarse a sí misma. Comúnmente hablan de la gracia preveniente de Dios como la gracia que capacita una respuesta real al Evangelio. Por tanto, la oferta de salvación puede ser aceptada o resistida; la fe no es producida por un decreto irresistible. Los calvinistas responden que la gracia salvadora lleva eficazmente a los elegidos a la fe. Ambas tradiciones procuran tomar en serio la enseñanza bíblica sobre la gracia, la fe, la incapacidad humana y la soberanía de Dios, pero relacionan esas verdades de manera diferente.

blocks.en: Perseverance, Security, and Apostasy: Christians also disagree about how to understand a person who once made a credible profession of faith, was received by the church as a brother or sister, but later abandons faith in Christ. Reformed theology teaches the Perseverance of the Saints: those truly regenerated by God will be preserved in faith to the end. From this perspective, final apostasy reveals that the earlier profession, however convincing it appeared, did not arise from genuine regeneration. Classical Arminian and Wesleyan theology allows a different explanation: the earlier faith may have been genuine, but the believer later abandoned that faith and fell from grace. Thus both traditions take apostasy seriously, but they differ over what the apostasy reveals about the person's earlier spiritual condition and over how divine sovereignty, preserving grace, human response, and continuing faith relate to one another. Other evangelical Christians combine an Arminian understanding of human response with eternal security. CTS does not require students to adopt one denominational system on this question. It does insist that salvation is entirely dependent on the grace of God in Christ, is received through faith, and that the New Testament repeatedly calls believers to continue trusting and following Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Perseverancia, Seguridad y Apostasía: Los cristianos también discrepan sobre cómo entender a una persona que una vez hizo una profesión de fe creíble, fue recibida por la iglesia como hermano o hermana, pero más tarde abandona la fe en Cristo. La teología Reformada enseña la Perseverancia de los Santos: quienes son verdaderamente regenerados por Dios serán preservados en la fe hasta el fin. Desde esta perspectiva, la apostasía final revela que la profesión anterior, por convincente que pareciera, no procedía de una regeneración genuina. La teología arminiana clásica y wesleyana permite una explicación diferente: la fe anterior pudo haber sido genuina, pero el creyente posteriormente abandonó esa fe y cayó de la gracia. Así, ambas tradiciones toman en serio la apostasía, pero difieren sobre lo que la apostasía revela acerca de la condición espiritual anterior de la persona y sobre cómo se relacionan entre sí la soberanía divina, la gracia preservadora, la respuesta humana y la fe continua. Otros cristianos evangélicos combinan una comprensión arminiana de la respuesta humana con la seguridad eterna. CTS no exige que los estudiantes adopten un sistema denominacional en esta cuestión. Sí insiste en que la salvación depende enteramente de la gracia de Dios en Cristo, se recibe por la fe, y que el Nuevo Testamento llama repetidamente a los creyentes a continuar confiando y siguiendo a Cristo.

blocks.en: The Charismatic and Pentecostal Expansion: Under the broader Arminian umbrella, we also find the groups that practice the Charismatic gifts. This includes Pentecostals, the Assemblies of God, and many other Charismatic groups. These groups elevate certain spiritual gifts, such as speaking in tongues and healing. Whether we agree with their specific practices or not, we know they are the fastest-growing groups in Christianity around the world. The Holy Spirit is certainly using the Charismatics, and we should be very careful about criticizing anyone whom the Holy Spirit is using.
blocks.es_reference: La Expansión Carismática y Pentecostal: Bajo el paraguas arminiano más amplio, también encontramos los grupos que practican los dones carismáticos. Esto incluye a los Pentecostales, las Asambleas de Dios y muchos otros grupos Carismáticos. Estos grupos elevan ciertos dones espirituales, como el hablar en lenguas y la sanidad. Estemos o no de acuerdo con sus prácticas específicas, sabemos que son los grupos de más rápido crecimiento en el cristianismo en todo el mundo. El Espíritu Santo ciertamente está usando a los Carismáticos, y debemos tener mucho cuidado al criticar a cualquiera a quien el Espíritu Santo esté usando.

blocks.en: Final Lessons
blocks.es_reference: Lecciones Finales

blocks.en: 1. Scripture Stands Above Tradition: This includes our own traditions. If there is a conflict, we must return to the New Testament model.
blocks.es_reference: 1. La Escritura está por encima de la Tradición: Esto incluye nuestras propias tradiciones. Si hay un conflicto, debemos volver al modelo del Nuevo Testamento.

blocks.en: 2. The Command of Missions: People without Christ are lost. Jesus said in Matthew 28:19-20: "Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them... and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age."
blocks.es_reference: 2. El Mandato de las Misiones: Las personas sin Cristo están perdidas. Jesús dijo en Mateo 28:19-20: "Por tanto, id, y enseñad a todas las naciones, bautizándoles... y he aquí yo estoy con vosotros todos los días, hasta el fin del mundo".

blocks.en: 3. Essential Doctrine Must Be Protected: The Gospel is not ours to improve or reshape. When the Gospel is changed, it is no longer the Gospel.
blocks.es_reference: 3. La Doctrina Esencial Debe Ser Protegida: El Evangelio no es nuestro para mejorarlo o remodelarlo. Cuando el Evangelio es cambiado, ya no es el Evangelio.

blocks.en: "If anyone preaches any other gospel to you than what you have received, let him be accursed." — Galatians 1:9
blocks.es_reference: "Si alguno os predica diferente evangelio del que habéis recibido, sea anatema." — Gálatas 1:9

blocks.en: "Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you." — Matthew 28:19-20
blocks.es_reference: "Por tanto, id, y enseñad a todas las naciones, bautizándoles en el nombre del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo; enseñándoles que guarden todas las cosas que os he mandado." — Mateo 28:19-20

blocks.en: Final Summary
blocks.es_reference: Resumen Final

blocks.en: The doctrine of denominations and authority teaches us that while the church was born in unity, differences developed over time. Not all differences are dangerous, but when the Gospel itself is redefined, it becomes another gospel altogether. The Catholic Church emphasizes tradition and papal authority. The Reformed tradition (Calvinism) emphasizes God's sovereignty and predestination. The Arminian tradition emphasizes God-enabled human response and resistible grace; many classical and Wesleyan Arminians also affirm the possibility of a genuine believer finally falling away from faith. The Charismatic and Pentecostal movements emphasize spiritual gifts and have become the fastest-growing Christian groups worldwide. Through all these traditions, Scripture must remain the final authority. The Gospel must be protected. And the mission to make disciples must never be abandoned.
blocks.es_reference: La doctrina de las denominaciones y la autoridad nos enseña que si bien la iglesia nació en unidad, con el tiempo se desarrollaron diferencias. No todas las diferencias son peligrosas, pero cuando el Evangelio mismo se redefine, se convierte en otro evangelio en absoluto. La Iglesia Católica enfatiza la tradición y la autoridad papal. La tradición Reformada (Calvinismo) enfatiza la soberanía de Dios y la predestinación. La tradición Arminiana enfatiza la respuesta humana capacitada por Dios y la gracia resistible; muchos arminianos clásicos y wesleyanos también afirman la posibilidad de que un verdadero creyente finalmente se aparte de la fe. Los movimientos Carismáticos y Pentecostales enfatizan los dones espirituales y se han convertido en los grupos cristianos de más rápido crecimiento en todo el mundo. A través de todas estas tradiciones, la Escritura debe seguir siendo la autoridad final. El Evangelio debe ser protegido. Y la misión de hacer discípulos nunca debe ser abandonada.

blocks.en: How Does Grace Reach the Sinner?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo Llega la Gracia al Pecador?

blocks.en: Two answers at the heart of the Reformation
blocks.es_reference: Dos respuestas en el corazón de la Reforma

blocks.en: The Catholic Answer
blocks.es_reference: La Respuesta Católica

blocks.en: Grace is mediated — it reaches the sinner through the Church and her sacraments.
blocks.es_reference: La gracia es mediada — llega al pecador por la Iglesia y sus sacramentos.

blocks.en: Grace is won by Christ — unmerited at its source.
blocks.es_reference: La gracia es ganada por Cristo — inmerecida en su origen.

blocks.en: It is conferred through the seven sacraments, beginning at baptism.
blocks.es_reference: Se confiere por los siete sacramentos, desde el bautismo.

blocks.en: The sacraments belong to the Church — she is the channel of grace.
blocks.es_reference: Los sacramentos pertenecen a la Iglesia — ella es el canal de la gracia.

blocks.en: The believer cooperates and merits within grace (faith and works).
blocks.es_reference: El creyente coopera y merece dentro de la gracia (fe y obras).

blocks.en: A treasury of merit — Christ and the saints — is held by the Church.
blocks.es_reference: La Iglesia guarda un tesoro de méritos — Cristo y los santos.

blocks.en: “Outside the Church there is no salvation.”
blocks.es_reference: “Fuera de la Iglesia no hay salvación.”

blocks.en: The Protestant Answer
blocks.es_reference: La Respuesta Protestante

blocks.en: Grace comes directly — it reaches the sinner through faith in Christ alone.
blocks.es_reference: La gracia llega directamente — al pecador por la fe en Cristo solamente.

blocks.en: By grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone (Eph 2:8–9).
blocks.es_reference: Por gracia sola, mediante fe sola, en Cristo solo (Ef 2:8–9).

blocks.en: Christ's finished work needs no supplement (Heb 10:14).
blocks.es_reference: La obra consumada de Cristo no necesita complemento (Heb 10:14).

blocks.en: One mediator between God and man — Christ (1 Tim 2:5).
blocks.es_reference: Un solo mediador entre Dios y los hombres — Cristo (1 Tim 2:5).

blocks.en: Every believer is a saint; no surplus merit, no treasury (Luke 17:10).
blocks.es_reference: Todo creyente es santo; sin mérito sobrante ni tesoro (Lc 17:10).

blocks.en: Baptism and the Supper proclaim the gospel; they do not confer grace.
blocks.es_reference: El bautismo y la Cena proclaman el evangelio; no confieren gracia.

blocks.en: The Church proclaims grace but is never its channel.
blocks.es_reference: La Iglesia proclama la gracia pero nunca es su canal.

blocks.en: THE REFORMATION'S VERDICT
blocks.es_reference: EL VEREDICTO DE LA REFORMA

blocks.en: When grace must pass through a required sacramental system, the rite itself becomes a work — so grace is no longer alone.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando la gracia debe pasar por un sistema sacramental obligatorio, el rito mismo se vuelve una obra — y la gracia ya no es sola.

blocks.es_reference: Cada lado se expone como él mismo enseña.

blocks.en: Who Stands Between God and Man?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Quién Está entre Dios y el Hombre?

blocks.en: Priesthood, mediation, and the torn veil
blocks.es_reference: El sacerdocio, la mediación y el velo rasgado

blocks.en: The Catholic Answer
blocks.es_reference: La Respuesta Católica

blocks.en: A ministerial priesthood mediates — ordained priests stand between God and the people.
blocks.es_reference: Un sacerdocio ministerial media — sacerdotes ordenados están entre Dios y el pueblo.

blocks.en: Priests are ordained to act in the person of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Los sacerdotes son ordenados para actuar en la persona de Cristo.

blocks.en: Only an ordained priest consecrates the Eucharist and absolves sins.
blocks.es_reference: Solo un sacerdote ordenado consagra la Eucaristía y absuelve pecados.

blocks.en: The faithful receive sacramental grace through the priesthood.
blocks.es_reference: Los fieles reciben la gracia sacramental por medio del sacerdocio.

blocks.en: Mary and the saints intercede for the faithful.
blocks.es_reference: María y los santos interceden por los fieles.

blocks.en: The Church and her priests share in Christ's mediation.
blocks.es_reference: La Iglesia y sus sacerdotes participan en la mediación de Cristo.

blocks.en: The Protestant Answer
blocks.es_reference: La Respuesta Protestante

blocks.en: One Mediator — Christ alone — and every believer a priest with direct access.
blocks.es_reference: Un solo Mediador — Cristo solo — y cada creyente sacerdote con acceso directo.

blocks.en: “One Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus” (1 Tim 2:5).
blocks.es_reference: “Un solo Mediador entre Dios y los hombres, Jesucristo hombre” (1 Tim 2:5).

blocks.en: Every believer is a priest — a holy and royal priesthood (1 Pet 2:5, 9).
blocks.es_reference: Todo creyente es sacerdote — un sacerdocio santo y real (1 Pe 2:5, 9).

blocks.en: We draw near to God directly, by the blood of Jesus (Heb 10:19–22).
blocks.es_reference: Nos acercamos a Dios directamente, por la sangre de Jesús (Heb 10:19–22).

blocks.en: No ordained caste stands between the believer and God.
blocks.es_reference: Ninguna casta ordenada está entre el creyente y Dios.

blocks.en: Christ alone intercedes — He ever lives to intercede (Heb 7:25).
blocks.es_reference: Solo Cristo intercede — vive siempre para interceder (Heb 7:25).

blocks.en: THE TORN VEIL
blocks.es_reference: EL VELO RASGADO

blocks.en: At the cross the veil was torn from top to bottom — opening a Holy of Holies that had stood empty for centuries.
blocks.es_reference: En la cruz el velo se rasgó de arriba abajo — abriendo un Lugar Santísimo que había estado vacío por siglos.

blocks.en: The way to God was thrown open, and the meeting place had moved to Christ Himself.
blocks.es_reference: El camino a Dios quedó abierto, y el lugar de encuentro se trasladó a Cristo mismo.

Before the Reformation, the Bible was often chained to the ____ to keep ordinary people from reading it.

The "Rock" of Matthew 16 is Peter's answer: Jesus is building His church not on a man, but on the truth of His own ____.

sa.prompt: Explain the difference between unity and uniformity. Why is this distinction important for understanding denominational differences?
sa.model: The unit distinguishes unity from uniformity. Uniformity would mean everyone looks, worships, and practices in exactly the same way, with no differences at all. Unity is a deeper oneness in the essentials of the faith that can hold together genuine diversity in secondary matters. The Bible calls for one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, but it does not demand that every congregation be identical. This distinction matters for understanding denominations because it lets us see that believers can differ on structure, worship style, and secondary doctrine while still being truly one in Christ. Denominational differences are not automatically a betrayal of unity; the church can be united in the core gospel while remaining diverse on the branches, like one family tree with many branches.

sa.prompt: Analyze Acts 15. How did the early church resolve doctrinal disagreement, and what can we learn from their process?
sa.model: In Acts 15 the unit shows the early church facing a serious doctrinal dispute and resolving it through a council. The leaders gathered together not to dominate one another but to discern the truth: they listened, they reasoned, they testified to what God had done, and they weighed the matter against Scripture before reaching a shared conclusion. We can learn several things from this process. Disagreement is handled openly and corporately, not by power plays or splits at the first sign of conflict. The aim is to discern truth, not to win, and Scripture is the standard that settles the question. The example teaches the church to face differences with humility, careful listening, and submission to God's Word, seeking unity in truth rather than either forced uniformity or careless division.

sa.prompt: Compare and contrast the Catholic understanding of Peter as the "rock" (Matthew 16) with the Protestant understanding.
sa.model: The unit contrasts two readings of Matthew 16. The Catholic understanding takes Peter himself to be the rock on which the church is built, making him the first pope so that church authority flows from him and his successors. The Protestant understanding looks again at the central issue in the passage, the question "Who do you say that I am?" On this reading the rock is Peter's confession, the revealed truth of who Jesus is, so that Christ builds His church on that confessed truth rather than on the man. Both agree the moment is foundational; they differ on what the foundation is. For Catholics it grounds an office of authority centered on Peter; for Protestants it grounds the church on the confession of Christ as the Son of God, with Christ Himself as the true foundation.

sa.prompt: Explain the five points of Calvinism (TULIP). What does each point teach?
sa.model: The unit lays out the five points of Calvinism under the acronym TULIP. Total Depravity teaches that man is so affected by sin that he cannot choose God on his own. Unconditional Election teaches that God chooses whom He will save based on His mercy rather than on anything in the person. Limited Atonement teaches that Christ died specifically for the elect. Irresistible Grace teaches that when God effectually calls, the soul will eventually respond. Perseverance of the Saints teaches that true believers will never finally fall away. Together these points present salvation as the work of God's sovereign grace from beginning to end, with God initiating, accomplishing, and securing the salvation of those He has chosen. They form an interlocking system emphasizing divine sovereignty in salvation.

sa.prompt: Explain the Arminian understanding of free will and the possibility of falling from grace. What concerns do Arminians emphasize?
sa.model: The unit presents classical Arminianism alongside Calvinism, emphasizing God-enabled human response and resistible grace. Where Calvinism teaches that those truly regenerated will finally persevere, classical and Wesleyan Arminians allow that a genuine believer may finally abandon faith. Both take apostasy seriously; they differ over what final apostasy reveals about the person’s earlier spiritual condition and how preserving grace and human response relate. Salvation therefore must be lived out with seriousness. Arminians emphasize human responsibility and the urgency of the call: if grace can be resisted and grace can be departed from, then the appeal to respond and to persevere carries real weight. The concern is to preserve genuine human accountability and the meaningfulness of the gospel invitation, guarding against any view that would make the call to faith and faithfulness empty.

sa.prompt: What was William Carey's contribution to missions, and why did he reject the hyper-Calvinist view of his day?
sa.model: The unit presents William Carey, a Baptist, as the father of modern missions. When he wanted to take the gospel to Asia, an older pastor reflecting the hyper-Calvinism of the day told him to sit down, saying that if God wanted to save the heathen He could do so without Carey's help. Carey refused that idea. He recognized that an over-pressed view of divine sovereignty had been twisted into an excuse for doing nothing, and he insisted that God's sovereignty does not cancel the church's responsibility to go and proclaim the gospel. His contribution was both practical and theological: he helped launch the modern missions movement, and he modeled a balance in which trusting God's sovereign purpose actually fuels rather than smothers active obedience to the Great Commission.

sa.prompt: What does it mean to be "non-denominational," and how can a non-denominational church avoid becoming "belief-less"?
sa.model: The unit explains that being non-denominational means not formally belonging to one of the established denominational structures, but it warns that this must not mean being belief-less. A church can decline a denominational label while still holding deep, grounded convictions about the core doctrines of the faith. The danger is that without a denominational heritage to anchor it, a church might drift into having no firm beliefs at all, treating doctrine as unimportant. The unit's answer is that non-denominational believers should keep deep, settled convictions even though they sit on a different branch of the same family tree. So the way to avoid being belief-less is to be clear and committed on the essentials of the gospel, recognizing oneself as part of the larger family of Christ rather than as a church without doctrine.

sa.prompt: Why does Paul say in Galatians 1:9 that those who preach another gospel should be "accursed" (anathema)? What does this reveal about the importance of the gospel?
sa.model: The unit explains Paul's severe language in Galatians 1:9 by pointing to what is at stake. Paul says that anyone who preaches another gospel should be accursed because the gospel is not ours to improve or reshape; it is God's saving message, fixed and given. The strength of the word anathema shows that this is not a secondary matter on which believers may agree to differ, but the very heart of the faith. This reveals that while denominations can differ in good conscience on many things, the core gospel is the one boundary that cannot be crossed. To distort the gospel is to endanger the only message by which people are saved. So Paul's harshness marks the line between secondary differences, which unity can absorb, and a corrupted gospel, which must be rejected outright.

sa.prompt: What should be the attitude of believers toward Charismatic and Pentecostal Christians, who are among the fastest-growing groups worldwide?
sa.model: The unit places Charismatic and Pentecostal Christians, including groups like the Assemblies of God, under the broader Arminian umbrella as those who practice the charismatic gifts, and notes they are among the fastest-growing groups worldwide. The fitting attitude flows from the unit's whole approach to denominations: where these believers hold the core gospel, they are brothers and sisters on another branch of the same family tree, to be treated with respect and recognized as fellow members of Christ's body, not as enemies. This does not erase real differences over the gifts or practice, which can be discussed honestly, but those secondary differences should not override the deeper unity. Given their size and growth, dismissing them would be both unkind and unwise; the unit's posture is humility, charity, and recognition of genuine fellow believers.

sa.prompt: Summarize the main point of Unit 9. How should Christians relate to those in different denominations?
sa.model: The main point of the unit is that the church is meant for unity, not uniformity: believers can differ on structure and secondary doctrine while remaining truly one in the essentials of the gospel. Denominations are like branches on a single family tree, and Christians should relate to those in other branches with humility, charity, and respect, recognizing genuine fellow believers wherever the core gospel is held. At the same time, there is one firm boundary: the gospel itself cannot be reshaped, so a corrupted gospel must be rejected even as secondary differences are tolerated. So Christians should hold their convictions seriously, discern disagreements carefully as the council in Acts 15 did, and love and honor believers across denominational lines, neither pretending all differences are unimportant nor breaking fellowship over matters that are not the gospel.
